rules.principle: The exact EU enforcement residue definition is authoritative for which components belong to the residue. Do not invent an analyte because it is the heading, a common name, in a catalogue family or a proposed risk-assessment residue. Parse the applicable commodity-specific (R) exception independently of the default.

For MRL enforcement, a marker may be parent, metabolite or analytical derivative. The identity of the pesticide used is NOT by itself a requirement that its parent be measured. Do not import broader dietary risk-assessment components into an enforcement definition.

rules.locator: OECD Scenario 1 pp. 31–32; Scenario 11 pp. 34; EU 2023/710 Chloridazon footnote
rules.principle: 'Expressed as X' normally identifies the substance used to express the reported quantity, potentially with mass conversion. It does not alone require measuring X. If 'X (Y, expressed as X)' identifies Y in the definition, include Y, not the heading X solely as an extra analyte. If the text actually says 'sum of X and Y', include both.
rules.origin: paraphrase of OECD with directly binding EU example

rules.locator: OECD Scenario 1 and 4 pp. 31–32; EU 2025/854 Article 2
rules.principle: Where the legal definition explicitly names a sum or mixture of distinguishable components, list each named constituent. Use a group only when the text specifies a structurally defined but nonenumerated class. Do not add the heading again when it merely labels the sum.

A measurement can determine several chemical forms through a single conversion product/common moiety. Distinguish the analyte ultimately determined from precursor forms and the compound used to express results. A conversion basis is not automatically an independently required parent analyte. Preserve any explicitly named precursors or nonenumerated group without guessing chemical identities.

'Free and conjugated', salts or unnamed esters usually qualify coverage of a named residue; do not invent a separately measured analyte for every unspecified form. Explicitly named, analytically distinct esters, salts or metabolites remain separately listed if the definition requires them.

rules.locator: Residue Definition for MRL Setting and Risk Assessment in the Case of Isomers, paragraphs 30–31, pp. 35–36
rules.principle: Treat an unnamed 'sum of isomers' as the aggregate for the named compound; do not hallucinate specific stereo forms. When the definition explicitly enumerates E/Z, cis/trans or R/S forms and separately measured terms exist, represent the named forms distinctly.

rules.locator: OECD Scenario 11, p. 34; EU Annex (R) footnote
rules.principle: Plant and livestock residues may have different marker analytes. Do not copy analytes from the default or plant definition into an animal exception unless that exception actually names them. Product scope is metadata, not an analyte.
rules.origin: paraphrase of OECD and EU source semantics

rules.locator: Exact active EU residue-definition text / (R) footnote
rules.principle: A conditional statement such as 'where only Y is detected, apply Y's residue definition' describes an alternative rule, not an additional analyte in the unconditional residue sum. Preserve the condition as a qualifier or annotation and do not silently treat both branches as simultaneously measured.
rules.origin: operational reading of EU legal wording; not a blanket legal interpretation

rules.locator: Exact active EU definition where the alternative name is in parentheses
rules.principle: An explicit alternate or former name is an identifier, not necessarily a second measured component. If there are separately listed biological strains or isomer identities, keep those distinct; do not collapse them just because a former name is also present.
rules.origin: operational rule for literal EU names

rules.locator: EU 2025/854 Article 2; EFSA 2026 ChemMon SSD2 scope; EFSA 2026 EU pesticide report methods
rules.principle: A whole legal RD PARAM identifier, an active-substance identifier and a separately reported analyte/part are different concepts. Only output the named components required by the EU definition; the deterministic PARAM mapper will link them. Do not choose a whole-RD code as a part merely because the label contains the same substance.
rules.origin: legal reporting instruction + EFSA publication context
